name: AML/goAML onboarding and CDD-record pack for small real estate agencies and law firms
buyer: Small estate agencies/property managers/landlords-as-agents and small law firms (advocates) that are POCAMLA reporting institutions; supervisors FRC and LSK
trigger: POCAMLA s.47A registration on goAML (real estate deadline 14 Nov 2025, passed); STR within days of suspicion (sources conflict 2 days / 7 working days / 3 days); cash >= USD 15,000 reporting; CDD on all buyers and sellers; 7-year record retention; FRC 2026 on-site inspection cycle (95% of legal and real estate profiled medium-high risk); 153 real estate agencies medium/high risk, 74 law firms.
evidence: https://www.businessdailyafrica.com/bd/economy/real-estate-law-firms-top-kenya-s-money-laundering-risk-list-5540984 ; https://cifar.eu/news/anti-money-laundering-rules-reporting-for-the-kenyan-real-estate-sector ; https://k24.digital/411/govt-issues-a-mandatory-directive-to-all-real-estate-agencies/amp ; https://fnjassociates.co.ke/suspicious-transaction-reporting-in-kenya/ ; 2024 FRC report: 1 STR from real estate out of 7,287 and none from lawyers (secondary, via search snippet).
existing: Competitor search ('goAML Kenya real estate agents law firms compliance software AML STR filing service FRC') found consultancies offering FRC registration help (e.g. fnjassociates.co.ke) and generic screening vendors (aiprise, checklynx); no Kenya-specific small-agency CDD/STR tool found, and no public goAML API (STR filing is by portal/XML). Swahili query not run.
unchecked: Whether small agents or only firms with full-time staff are in scope; LSK supervision regime for advocates; what the FRC portal already offers (templates, guidance); exact STR deadline; willingness to pay; overlap with generic AML tools.

first_check.duty: POCAMLA 2009 as amended (2023, 2025) and the POCAMLA Regulations 2023. Real estate agents (selling, mortgaging, letting or managing immovable property) and advocates acting for clients in property, client-funds or company and trust work are reporting institutions. Duties: register with the FRC on goAML (s.47A; failing to register is an offence under s.47A(5); the agents' deadline was 14 Nov 2025 and has passed); CDD/EDD (PEPs, beneficial owners); an MLRO and internal AML system; STRs (secondary sources say within 7 working days; not confirmed from the statute); weekly Friday reports to the FRC on deals over USD 15,000, with buyer identity and source of income; 7-year record retention. Penalties: up to KSh25m for institutions, KSh5m for individuals, KSh10,000 a day for up to 180 days. LSK is the self-regulatory body for advocates. Its Legal Sector Guidelines were approved in Oct 2025, and it added a Law Firm Statistical Questionnaire in June 2026 (submitted by email as a PDF).
first_check.market: Estate agents: the FRC targeted 1,504 agents for registration, and 112 had registered by late Oct 2025. An undated EARB figure puts registered agents at about 3,000, and more than 40,000 unregistered agents are said to operate. Advocates: about 23,000 practising LSK members and about 27,000 enrolled (late 2025), though only those doing covered work are in scope. The claim's risk-profiled figures (153 agencies, 74 law firms rated medium/high risk) come from the cited Business Daily article, which I did not re-check.
first_check.competitor: I found no Kenya-specific CDD/STR/goAML workflow tool for small estate agencies or law firms. Nearby options: YouVerify and Smile ID (KYC/AML aimed at banks and CBK-regulated firms), AML Guard (Nairobi, founded 2025; serves casinos, insurers and gaming), CheckLynx (sanctions screening), and consultancies such as FNJ Associates that help with FRC registration. LSK's free AML/CFT/CPF Compliance Hub offers a template policy, due-diligence guidance, STR red-flag notes, TFS circulars and a statistical questionnaire, but no software or portal. STRs are filed on the FRC's goAML portal. I did not check whether it supports XML or batch upload.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and in force. Under POCAMLA s.47A, estate agents (selling, letting or managing property) and advocates are reporting institutions. They must register on goAML, carry out CDD and EDD, appoint an MLRO, file STRs, keep records for 7 years and report weekly (every Friday, per Business Daily) on property deals over USD 15,000. Fines run to KSh25m for institutions and KSh5m for individuals, plus KSh10,000 a day. I found no Kenya-specific small-firm CDD/STR tool. LSK's free hub gives template policies, guidance and a questionnaire but no software. Weak points: only 112 of 1,504 targeted agents had registered, the FRC did 44 DNFBP inspections against a target of 487, and firms seem unlikely to pay. The STR deadline is still unclear: secondary sources say 7 working days and one template says 3. Not checked: whether goAML offers XML or batch upload.

challenge_check.killer: None found. Partial threats: First AML and Realaml (law-firm KYC workflow tools from New Zealand), Sumsub/YouVerify generic KYC, and consultancies such as FNJ Associates.
challenge_check.reason: I found no product that kills this. No Kenya-specific CDD/STR/goAML tool for small estate agencies or law firms turned up. The nearest options are foreign or generic: First AML and Realaml (New Zealand, law-firm KYC, with no sign of Kenya configuration), Sumsub, YouVerify and Smile ID (aimed at banks and fintechs), and AML Guard (casinos, insurers and gaming). The duty does bite. An LSK FAQ dated August 2026 says it applies to all private-practice advocates, sole practitioners included, and the FRC has set a 2026 inspection cycle. Limits: the market is small (the FRC targeted 1,504 real estate agents, only 112 had registered at the time of reporting, and only conveyancing advocates are in scope), willingness to pay is weak, and global tools could expand into this space. I did not run Swahili queries, and the LSK FAQ was unreadable.
